name: Allopurinol
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: Start 100 mg daily; increase by 100 mg weekly to serum urate 6 mg/dL or less; maximum 800 mg daily

key_interactions.effect: Higher risk of skin rash and hypersensitivity; kidney impairment adds to the risk.
key_interactions.action: Monitor kidney function and reduce the allopurinol dose in kidney impairment; stop at the first rash.

key_interactions.effect: Allopurinol blocks their metabolism; more myelosuppression.
key_interactions.action: With allopurinol 300 to 600 mg/day, cut the azathioprine or mercaptopurine dose to about one-third to one-fourth.

key_interactions.effect: Lower levels of capecitabine's active metabolites; may reduce efficacy.
key_interactions.action: Do not use allopurinol during capecitabine treatment.

key_interactions.effect: Can blunt the urate rise that signals loss of response and raise anaphylaxis risk.
key_interactions.action: Stop and do not start allopurinol during pegloticase.
Check cyclosporine levels more often and adjust its dose.

key_interactions.effect: Longer chlorpropamide half-life (competing tubular excretion); hypoglycemia risk in renal insufficiency.
key_interactions.action: Monitor for hypoglycemia in kidney impairment.
Monitor prothrombin time and adjust the anticoagulant.

key_interactions.effect: More skin rash, which may be severe.
key_interactions.action: Stop allopurinol at the first rash or sign of hypersensitivity.

common: Raised alkaline phosphatase, AST or ALT (≥1%)
serious: Severe skin reactions and hypersensitivity, sometimes fatal

contraindications: Hypersensitivity to allopurinol or any ingredient
monitoring: HLA-B*58:01: consider testing before starting in patients of Southeast Asian (including Filipino), Han Chinese, Korean, Thai, African or Pacific Islander ancestry; avoid allopurinol in carriers unless benefit clearly outweighs risk (label 5.1; ACR 2020). CKD increases the risk of severe hypersensitivity.
Before starting: serum urate, complete blood count, chemistry panel, liver tests, serum creatinine and eGFR (label)
Serum urate during titration (target 6 mg/dL or less)
Skin rash or other hypersensitivity signs

pk.half_life: Allopurinol 1 to 2 hours; oxipurinol about 15 hours
pk.half_life_eskd: Oxipurinol half-life markedly prolonged in kidney failure (label gives no figure; exposure rises steeply as eGFR falls, 8.6).
pk.metabolism: Converted to oxipurinol (oxypurinol), also a xanthine oxidase inhibitor
pk.excretion_renal_pct: Renal (oxipurinol unchanged in urine by filtration and tubular reabsorption); about 20% of the dose in feces
pk.dialyzability: Yes: allopurinol and oxipurinol are dialyzable; value in overdose unknown (label).
